content.title: Navigation Should Describe Intent
content.hook: In a web application, a navigation control should make its destination understandable.
content.context:
Conceptually:

```jsx
<Link to="/products">Products</Link>
```

The important part is not memorizing one library API. The important part is that the control communicates a destination.
goals: Distinguish navigation from arbitrary click behavior and choose navigation mechanisms that communicate where the user is going.

content.question: Which control best expresses “go to the account page”?

options.text: A navigation link with an explicit destination.
A button whose click handler secretly changes the address.
A paragraph with a hidden click listener.
A timer that waits three seconds and changes the page.

feedback.correct: Navigation is a user-visible intent. The control should communicate that intent rather than hide the destination inside unrelated behavior.
feedback.incorrect: Navigation is a user-visible intent. The control should communicate that intent rather than hide the destination inside unrelated behavior.

activities.title: Buttons do things; links go places

content.title: Buttons do things; links go places
content.text:
This is a useful rule of thumb:

**Link → navigation**

**Button → action**

The distinction matters because users build expectations around controls.

content.question:
A navigation bar has links for:

```text
Home | Products | Account
```

The user is currently on `/account`.

What should the application make clear?

options.text: Only the first link is important.
The current location should be visually or semantically identifiable.
Every link should look identical in every state.

feedback.correct: Users should be able to understand where they are, not just where they could go.
feedback.incorrect: Users should be able to understand where they are, not just where they could go.

content.question:
A developer says, “I can make any clickable element navigate, so semantics do not matter.”

What is the better response?

options.text: The meaning of the control matters because navigation and actions have different user expectations and accessibility consequences.

feedback.correct: Engineering is not only about whether the browser can make something work. The interface should communicate the intended behavior.
feedback.incorrect: Engineering is not only about whether the browser can make something work. The interface should communicate the intended behavior.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** Navigation should look and behave like navigation.
**Senior habit:** Before wiring a click, name the intent: “go somewhere” or “do something.” That choice often determines the correct control.

requirements: Screen-reader accessible code blocks and options
